I published `jacobianData_of_subsingleton` as "a second route to `JacobianData` with none of
the three atlas antecedents", backed by an enumeration of seven producers said to all consume
the same chart family. A `work-reviewer` audit refuted it three ways at once (I-1573):

- **my own definition's body was `JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy` applied to a new `rep`.** So

**Why:** an absence census aimed at the GOAL passes even when the thing you built is one level
below it. Every mechanism-level check (build, sorries, axioms, binder deletion) is blind to the
difference between "no producer of the goal" and "no producer of this field of the goal".

**How to apply:** before writing a headline of the form "the first/only X", (1) read your own
proof term and name the constructor it calls — if that constructor is the goal's general one,
your result belongs to its *argument*, not to the goal; (2) census producers by **conclusion
shape**, `grep` for the type you actually inhabit, and include the general constructor in the
list. Related: [[witness-is-not-producer]], [[census-the-carrier-target-pair]],
[[absence-claims-rest-on-scans-not-censuses]], [[scoreboard-of-antecedents-has-no-goal]].

- I wrote "the debt becomes a statement about RINGS" while the bridging lemma's own docstring,
